guarantees.claim: For each share i, a prim_slicer instance is generated with InW=MaxEncodedKeyW+16, IndexW=KeccakMsgAddrW, OutW=MsgWidth, connecting sel_i=key_index, data_i=encoded_key_block[i], and data_o=key_sliced[i].
guarantees.cond: always when generate block is active

assumptions.claim: encoded_key_block[i] must be exactly MaxEncodedKeyW+16 bits wide.
assumptions.risk: Width mismatch may cause synthesis error or undefined slicing behavior.

assumptions.claim: key_index must select a MsgWidth-bit slice that lies entirely within the InW input (i.e., key_index must not cause out-of-range access).
assumptions.risk: Out-of-range selection may output X, zero, or wrap-around data, potentially leaking or corrupting key material.

assumptions.claim: Consumer of key_sliced[i] expects exactly MsgWidth bits per slice.
assumptions.risk: Width mismatch may cause downstream synthesis errors or data corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: key_index (KeccakMsgAddrW bits wide) may take values that select a slice beyond the MaxEncodedKeyW+16 input, and it is unclear if the prim_slicer or surrounding logic handles this safely.
uncertain_points.cond: when key_index selects a slice that exceeds InW bounds
uncertain_points.risk: Could produce undefined output, exposing or corrupting secret key slices.

uncertain_points.claim: The input width MaxEncodedKeyW+16 adds an extra 16 bits; the purpose is not documented, possibly related to padding or additional metadata.
uncertain_points.risk: Misunderstanding the extra bits could lead to incorrect slicing assumptions or security gaps.
